Short answer: it's probably worth collapsing to one path, but removing the bridge won't fix this bug.

**What's actually wrong.** The bridge works fine. The problem is that `cp` sends the copy to the wrong server. Your primary server is `station76`, but `sbx_fepr7496gy6bmvty` is on `beenie` (the local unix socket). `cp`, `tools ssh`, `shell` and `tools run` only ever look up a bare ID or name on the primary server. A full `sbx_…` ID isn't checked at all, so ssh logs in as that sandbox on station76. Station76 has no such sandbox, so its sshd rejects the key, and that shows up as `Permission denied (publickey)`.

`ssh sbx_…` works because the generated ssh_config sets `--server unix:///run/user/1002/discobox/server.sock` for each host. What I checked:
- `discobox --server unix:///run/user/1002/discobox/server.sock cp … sbx_fepr7496gy6bmvty:/tmp/t.txt` succeeds.
- `discobox tools ssh sbx_fepr…` fails with the same publickey error.
- `discobox shell sbx_fepr…` fails with `404 sandbox not found`.

This breaks ADR 0116 §4, which says a bare discobox ID is looked up on the primary and then on the registered servers. Only `selectSandbox` does that today; `resolveShellTarget` and `resolveCPTarget` don't.

A ProxyCommand-based `cp` would hit the same bug, because it would still need to know which server to name. The resolution fix is needed either way.

**Is the bridge worth keeping?** I'd lean towards removing it and using `-o ProxyCommand=<self> --server <resolved> admin ssh-proxy`, the same path your ssh_config already uses:
- **What goes away:**
  - the loopback listener, which is an unauthenticated local port onto sshd while a command runs;
  - the temporary known_hosts file pinned to a random port (a fixed `HostKeyAlias` would replace it);
  - a second code path that behaves slightly differently.
- **What it costs:**
  - one short-lived `discobox` process per ssh connection, which only matters for `scp -3`, since that opens two;
  - passing `--server`, plus `--token` if one was given, into the ProxyCommand line;
  - quoting on Windows, where the ssh-config path already has to get that right.

My suggestion is two commits:
1. **Fix resolution:** make `resolveShellTarget` and `cp` search every registered server. Split `selectSandbox`'s cross-server picker out so all of them share it, and have `cp` refuse operands that land on two different servers, as it already does for addresses. Add tests next to `TestSelectSandboxFindsAnIDOnWhicheverServerHasIt`.
2. **Replace the bridge with ProxyCommand** in `cp` and `tools ssh`, and delete `sshBridge`.

Launch a prompt in a new discobox against the current directory.

The prompt is the words after this command, or -p to give it as one argument.
Use -- when the words need to be separated from command flags explicitly. This is
the only command that makes a discobox: the bare "discobox" takes no prompt and
none of these flags.

By default new opens the console's window and makes the discobox there: the
question about uncommitted work is asked on it, the wait is drawn on it, and
what it lands on is the discobox itself — its default terminal (the configured
harness, or a shell when it has none), the shells and services running beside
it, and its forwarded ports. It is the same screen, in the same window, that
typing the same thing into "discobox console" gives you. Press Ctrl-A d to leave,
which detaches and exits; the discobox and everything in it keeps running
(DISCOBOX_LEADER changes the Ctrl-A).

--raw creates the discobox here instead and attaches this terminal to its
default terminal: the stream and nothing else, for a pipe, a recording, or a
terminal you would rather keep as it is. The questions are asked on this
terminal, one per source. Ctrl-A d detaches there too. If an interrupt stops
getting through — the discobox or the server has gone quiet — Ctrl-C again says
so, and one more quits, leaving the terminal running like a detach. Without a
terminal to draw a window on, new is raw whether or not the flag was given.

Pass -d to create the discobox and print it without attaching at all; there is
no window in that either.

Uncommitted changes in the source directory are carried into the discobox as a
snapshot on top of the checked-out commit. By default new asks before doing that
when there is a terminal to ask on; --include-dirty=true|false answers ahead of
time.

The source keeps its own path inside the discobox, so /home/you/src/app is
/home/you/src/app in there too. That holds for a directory under /home, /Users,
/mnt, /workspace, /Volumes, /media, /srv, /opt, /data or /var/home; everywhere
else the discobox's own system owns the path, so the source is placed at
/workspace/source instead and the discobox starts in the same subdirectory you
ran from. A source at one of those roots itself, or under /opt/discobox, is
placed that way too.

A source directory that is not in a Git repository works too: everything in it
is carried into the discobox as uncommitted changes on an empty first commit,
and nothing is written to the directory itself. Because that is the whole
directory, new asks first — with the size it would copy, counted while the
question is on screen — and not copying is the default answer: the discobox is
still created, with nothing checked out in it, exactly as --no-source does.
--include-dirty=true|false answers this one ahead of time too.

--no-source creates a discobox with nothing checked out in it, for work that
starts from an empty machine rather than from a repository. The directory you
run in is still what the discobox is filed under, so it is listed here like any
other, and the Git authorship it commits under is still read from here; only the
source is left out. -i still brings sources in, so --no-source -i ../foo is a
discobox holding foo and nothing else.

-i brings extra sources into the same discobox, repeat it for more than one. Each
is resolved exactly like the source directory is, uncommitted changes included,
and a local one keeps its own absolute path inside the discobox, so ../foo shows
up at the path readlink -f ../foo prints, under the same rule the source
directory follows above; one from anywhere else is placed under /workspace,

Fix: `discobox cp`, `tools ssh`, `shell`, and `tools run` ignore registered servers, then replace the SSH loopback bridge with ProxyCommand. Do it as two commits on the current branch.

## Bug (reproduced on the host)

`discobox cp go.work sbx_fepr7496gy6bmvty:` fails with `sbx_...@127.0.0.1: Permission denied (publickey)`. Plain `ssh sbx_...` and `sftp sbx_...` work, going through the ssh_config that `discobox admin ssh-config` writes.

Root cause: the primary server (`discobox admin remote`) is a remote server (station76). The discobox is on a registered server (beenie, the local unix socket). `resolveCPTarget`/`resolveCPSandbox` (cli/internal/cli/cp.go) and `resolveShellTarget` (cli/internal/cli/shell.go, used by shell, tools ssh, tools run) only resolve a bare name or ID against the **primary**. A full generated ID is trusted with no lookup at all. So the ssh bridge dials the primary's sshd with user `sbx_...`, `publicKeyCallback` (server/internal/sshd/server.go) finds no such sandbox, and the client sees a publickey rejection. What I observed:
- `discobox --server unix:///run/user/1002/discobox/server.sock cp ...`: works
- `discobox tools ssh sbx_fepr...`: same publickey failure
- `discobox shell sbx_fepr...`: `404 sandbox not found`

This breaks ADR 0116 §4: "A command given a bare discobox ID asks the primary first and the registered servers after." Only `selectSandbox` (cli/internal/cli/picker.go) follows it today, via `findOnEveryServer` (cli/internal/cli/servers.go).

## Commit 1: resolve references across every server

- When more than one server is known (`a.servers()`), `resolveShellTarget` must:
  - send a full generated ID through `findOnEveryServer`;
  - match a name or short ID against the cross-server `discobox ls` candidates (`sandboxCandidates`) with `matchSandboxArg`'s rules (configuredName), routed to the matching row's server;
  - fall back to the cross-server picker when nothing matches.
  Keep shell's existing semantics: an unmatched non-ID argument is the command.
- `cp` without an address: resolve each distinct reference the same way.
  - A short ID that matches no directory candidate still goes project-wide, via `findOnEveryServer`.
  - A name that matches nothing is an error, as `resolveSandboxReference` makes it.
  - A bare `:PATH` uses the cross-server picker, with cp's own picker wording ("name one before the colon").
  - Operands landing on two different servers are refused, like the existing "one copy reaches one server" check for addresses.
- Split the picker half of `selectSandbox` into a shared helper that takes the already-fetched candidates, so the listing isn't fetched twice, and callers pass their own empty/ambiguous messages. Consider having `findOnEveryServer` and the picker helper return `*server` rather than `*App`, so errors can name servers.
- Single-server behavior stays as it is.
- Tests go in cli/internal/cli/servers_list_test.go, next to `TestSelectSandboxFindsAnIDOnWhicheverServerHasIt` / `TestShellTargetRoutesAnAddress` / `TestCPRoutesAnAddress`, using `fakeServer` + `registerForTest`. Cover: an ID on a registered server (shell and cp), a name on a registered server, and cp refusing operands on two servers.

## Commit 2: remove the loopback bridge; use ProxyCommand

`cp` and `tools ssh` currently open a loopback TCP listener (`sshBridge` in cli/internal/cli/ssh_bridge.go) plus a temp known_hosts pinned to that random port. The emitted ssh_config already reaches the same sshd through `ProxyCommand '<discobox>' --server '<server>' admin ssh-proxy` (cli/internal/cli/ssh_proxy.go). Collapse to that one path:
- Build the ssh/scp args with `-o ProxyCommand=...` naming this executable (`os.Executable`) and the resolved server's address, the one the discobox is on, from commit 1. Carry `--token` or other needed transport settings the way the resolved App would need them; check what `forServer` does and doesn't carry.
- Use a fixed `HostKeyAlias` (the ssh-config writer uses `<project>.discobox.internal`; match it) with a temp or pinned known_hosts, instead of the per-port `[127.0.0.1]:port` entry. Keep `-F none`, `IdentitiesOnly=yes`, and `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes`. Keep the Windows percent/space-safe spelling (`sshConfigPath`) for values that go through `-o`, and make sure the ProxyCommand quoting works on Windows too. Reuse whatever quoting the ssh-config writer already has.
- `scp -3` (discobox to discobox) must still work: each end runs its own ProxyCommand.
- Delete `sshBridge`, `startSSHBridge`, and the bridge-specific pieces. Keep `sshConnectDialer`, which ssh-proxy uses. Update comments, `cp`/`tools ssh` help text ("through a loopback port that exists only while the command runs"), and any DESIGN.md that describes the bridge (grep for "bridge" under cli/ and docs/).
- Update or replace the tests that cover the bridge args (cp_test.go, tools ssh tests).

Read DESIGN.md/REVIEW.md root-down to cli/internal/cli first. Run `go tool task check-hooks` before finishing. Commit with clear messages; don't push.
EOF
